sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Departmental Undertakings**: Oldest form of public enterprise, directly managed by a government ministry as an extension of the government (e.g., Indian Railways, Post Office).
• **Statutory Corporations**: Formed by a special Act of Parliament or State Legislature, possessing independent legal identity and financial autonomy (e.g., LIC, RBI, FCI).
• **Government Companies**: Registered under the Companies Act (2013 or previous 1956 Act) where the government holds at least 51% of the paid-up share capital (e.g., ONGC, NTPC, BHEL).
• **Key Metric / Financial Autonomy**: Delegation of enhanced financial and operational powers to CPSEs based on profit performance, net worth, and export-import orientation.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Elite club of mega-PSUs with global presence (e.g., ONGC, IOCL, NTPC, Coal India).
Must be a Navratna, listed on SEBI stock exchange, average annual net profit > Rs. 5,000 cr for 3 years.
Board can invest up to Rs. 5,000 cr or 15% of net worth in a single project without prior govt approval.
High-performing enterprises with comparative global advantage (e.g., BEL, HAL, GAIL).
Must have 'Schedule A' status and 'Excellent' or 'Very Good' MoU rating in 3 of the last 5 years.
Board can invest up to Rs. 1,000 cr without govt clearance; freedom to form joint ventures abroad.
Profitable enterprises split into Category-I and Category-II based on continuous profits and net worth.
Category-I: Made profit for last 3 years continuously and positive net worth. Category-II: Positive net worth and profit for last 3 years.
Category-I boards can incur capital expenditure up to Rs. 500 cr or equal to net worth.

items.definition: Currently under the Ministry of Finance (shifted from Ministry of Heavy Industries in 2021); acts as the nodal agency for all Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs).
High-powered body constituted by the Government of India to recommend appointments for top management posts (Chairperson, Managing Director, Whole-time Director) in CPSEs.
An instrument of performance evaluation where quantitative and qualitative targets are agreed upon annually between the administrative ministry and the CPSE management.

items.term: New Public Sector Enterprise Policy for Non-Strategic Sectors
items.definition: Announced under Aatmanirbhar Bharat package; classifies sectors into Strategic (bare minimum presence) and Non-Strategic (privatization, merger, or closure).

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Resource-Rich Belts**: Heavy concentration of mining, metallurgical, and heavy engineering CPSEs in Eastern and Central India (Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal).
• **Strategic & High-Tech Clusters**: Aerospace, defense, and electronics manufacturing CPSEs concentrated in Southern and Western hubs (Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune) due to research ecosystems and historical defense industrial parks.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Bureaucratic red-tapism, delayed decision-making, overstaffing, legacy asset overhang, and sub-optimal capacity utilization in select manufacturing units.
• **Policy Interventions**: Strategic Disinvestment Policy, Asset Monetization Pipeline, professionalization of boards through independent directors, and competitive neutrality.

items.title: Mnemonic for CPSE Status Hierarchy
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'My Naive Mother'
• **Decoded Meaning**: **M**aharatna (Top) -> **N**avratna (Middle) -> **M**iniratna (Base).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly recalls financial power gradation and qualification criteria hierarchy.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Maharatna requires List + Net Worth > Rs. 15,000 cr + Turnover > Rs. 25,000 cr + Net Profit > Rs. 5,000 cr (all average for 3 years).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often frames statements claiming all Government Companies are Statutory Corporations. Remember: Statutory Corporations are formed via special Acts (e.g., LIC), whereas Government Companies are registered under the Companies Act (e.g., ONGC).

Mains Value Addition: Use the argument of 'Commercial Autonomy vs. Social Accountability' while writing answers on PSE reforms. Quote the Arjun Sengupta Committee recommendations on functional autonomy.

keyTakeaways: PSUs are structurally divided into Departmental Undertakings, Statutory Corporations, and Government Companies based on formation and legislative control.
Financial autonomy is categorized into Maharatna, Navratna, and Miniratna based on strict financial benchmarks like net profit, net worth, and turnover.
The modern economic policy shifts PSEs toward strategic sectors via privatization, asset monetization, and competitive efficiency under the New PSE Policy.
